subject.title: Feature: Multi-index embedding memory with model-aware failover (no mixed vector spaces)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class multi-index embedding memory now, and should that contract live in memory-core, a plugin API extension, or an external memory plugin?
rationale: The request changes public config, SQLite index layout, ingestion coordination, provider failover policy, observability, and migration behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API or rollout plan.

options.title: Design core/API contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open and have the memory owner define the multi-index config, storage, migration, status, and plugin-boundary contract before implementation.

options.title: Route to plugin-owned memory
options.body: If maintainers want this outside bundled memory-core, define the missing plugin seam and let an external memory plugin own multi-index failover.

options.title: Defer broad failover
options.body: Keep the existing identity guard and only fix narrower provider recovery bugs such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96534 for now.

recommendation.title: Design core/API contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and have the memory owner define the multi-index config, storage, migration, status, and plugin-boundary contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is the current issue assignee and the best available owner for deciding the product/API direction.
